record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Suppose L is a finitely generated group with Π^0_1 word problem that is effectively residually finite in the sense of Theorem 14. Investigate the following: (a) can such a group have unsolvable word problem; (b) is there a finitely generated residually finite Π-group that is not effectively residually finite; and (c) Morozov constructed a Π-group not isomorphic to a subgroup of S_rec, and can one build such a group so that it is also residually finite?

evidence.quote: A f.g. group S = Fk/N is effectively residually finite (e.r.f.) if there is an algorithm that, on input w ∈ Fk, in case w /∈ N computes a finite group Q and homomorphism r : Fk → Q such that r(N) = {e} and r(w) ≠ e.

Problem 15. (a) Can such a group L have unsolvable word problem? (b) Is there a f.g., residually finite Π-group that is not effectively r.f.? (c) Morozov ... constructed a Π-group that is not isomorphic to a subgroup of Srec. Can we make such a group r.f.?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the free group F_k of rank k with the standard generating set. For a normal subgroup N ⊴ F_k, call the finitely generated group S = F_k/N a Π-group if N is a Π^0_1 (co-recursively enumerable) subset of F_k, equivalently if the set of words representing the identity has a co-r.e. presentation.

Call a finitely generated group S = F_k/N effectively residually finite (e.r.f.) if there exists an algorithm which, on input a word w ∈ F_k with w ∉ N, computes a finite group Q and a homomorphism r : F_k → Q such that r(N) = {e_Q} and r(w) ≠ e_Q. (Note that an e.r.f. group is automatically residually finite, and its non-identity words can be effectively detected; the word problem is r.e. — together with Π^0_1 this would give decidability.)

Recall S_rec denotes the group of computable permutations of ℕ.

Answer the following three questions:

(a) Does there exist a finitely generated group L which is a Π-group and effectively residually finite (in the above sense) but whose word problem is undecidable?

(b) Does there exist a finitely generated residually finite Π-group that is not effectively residually finite?

(c) There exists a finitely generated Π-group that is not isomorphic to any subgroup of S_rec. Can such a Π-group additionally be required to be residually finite?
artifact.category_tag: Computable group theory / residually finite groups
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Darbinyan–Rauzy and collaborators, 2025) constructs robust families of residually finite groups with various computability properties and addresses distinctions between residual finiteness and effective residual finiteness, but it is not clear from publicly available abstracts/summaries that all three parts (a), (b), (c) of this specific problem have been resolved. Part (a) is suggested by general principles to be impossible (e.r.f. combined with Π^0_1 word problem yields decidability), but the explicit formulation here remains as posed. Status overall is unclear from public sources.

status_evidence.title: A robust family of residually finite groups; spectra of residual finiteness growth, computability properties, and other applications
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs residually finite groups with controlled computability properties, including discussion distinguishing residual finiteness from effective residual finiteness.
status_evidence.claim: Recent constructions distinguish residually finite and effectively residually finite groups, relevant to part (b).

status_evidence.title: Obstruction to a Higman embedding theorem for residually finite groups with solvable word problem
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses interactions between residual finiteness, word problem solvability, and embedding theorems.
status_evidence.claim: Related background on the interplay between residual finiteness and word problem decidability.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the three-part Problem 15 about effectively residually finite Π-groups.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as open in a 2025 problem list.
